provenance.rightsNote: Lectio Edition (SDIT): clear modern English of Augustine's Confessions, synthesized from the public-domain translation tradition (Pusey 1838; Watts 1631) and checked against the Latin; modern critical translations consulted, not quoted. In progress, book by book.
sourcesCited: Latin, the original text of the Confessiones
E. B. Pusey, The Confessions of S. Augustine (1838, public domain)
F. J. Sheed (1942, consulted, not quoted)

character: Plain modern English — the sense of the original, made to read with ease today.
overview: The Lectio Edition renders Augustine's Confessions in plain modern English that keeps its prayerful urgency and restless intelligence — sin and conversion, memory and time, a heart that finds no rest until it rests in God — while shedding the archaic diction.
introduction: The Confessions is the first true autobiography of an inner life: Augustine talking directly to God, and letting us overhear. It moves from a misspent youth through a long intellectual and moral struggle to conversion, then turns to memory, time, and the meaning of Genesis. Read it as one long prayer thinking out loud.
